findings.title: Cleanup can re-add a member after a concurrent delete
findings.why_it_matters: After cleanup removes an orphan, a concurrent InsertEntry can recreate the value; if cleanup's EXISTS sees it, a concurrent DeleteEntry can then delete the value and remove its member before cleanup's final ZAddNX. Cleanup leaves a stale directory member behind, so the next listing retries and cleans it again. Repeated interleavings can keep reintroducing names the intent is meant to remove.
findings.first_evidence: weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store.go:237-251 — removeOrphanedDirectoryListMember does ZREM; if it succeeds, checks EXISTS; on a live key it issues ZAddNX.
evidence: weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store.go:56-74 — InsertEntry writes the value before adding the directory member.
weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store.go:119-143 — DeleteEntry deletes the value and removes its parent directory member.
weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store.go:237-251 — orphan cleanup's existence check and conditional ZAddNX are separate commands.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the existence check and conditional ZAddNX atomic with respect to DeleteEntry, for example by using a Redis-side script for the cleanup check/add and ensuring the delete's value/member removal cannot interleave between them.
